subject: SIG: clarifying tenant-facing audit log slices & timebound access
body:
From: Terry Alfaro <terry.alfaro@finbank.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@procure.finbank.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: SIG follow-up: tenant log slices and short-lived access request

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for filing the SIG. A few compliance reviewers at FinBank had follow-ups specifically about audit-log handling:

- We need an example of the minimal "slice" of tenant events you can export (fields + retention window) for e-discovery requests. Is that a CSV/JSON sample you can provide?
- For higher-sensitivity incidents, would you support timebound (one-hour / one-day) scoped access to raw event streams for our auditors? We need the request -> approval -> access audit trail captured.
- What is Redwood's SLA for exporting historical logs older than 180 days? Our procurement team is also asking about any cost or lead time.

Can you point us to the exact playbook and attach a sample export so we can validate the schema against our internal pipeline?

Thanks,
Terry
Senior Compliance Manager, FinBank

---

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Terry Alfaro <terry.alfaro@finbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 11:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: tenant log slices and short-lived access request

Hi Terry — thank you for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (security/evidence) and Neha (support/ops) to confirm operational steps. High-level answers here, details and artifacts attached.

1) Minimal slice sample: attached is a redwood-audit-log-sample-202706.zip (CSV + JSON schema). The minimal slice we normally produce contains: timestampUTC, tenant_id, request_id, model_id, route, response_latency_ms, outcome_code, auth_subject, ip_country, kv_cache_hit (true/false). We can generate additional columns on request (full request/response payloads require explicit customer authorization).

2) Timebound auditor access: Yes — we support scoped, time-limited access via an ephemeral credential flow. Process:
   - Customer opens a support ticket with requested window and justification.
   - Security reviews and issues an approval token (signed) linked to the support ticket.
   - Support provisions a one-time credential (expires after the window) which is auditable (ticket id + approver).
   - All access is recorded in the same audit log and lodged in the export bundle.

We attach our timebound-access-playbook-v1.2.pdf explaining the flow and sample approval record.

3) Export SLA for >180d logs: Standard turn-around is 10 business days for >180d cold exports; expedited (2 business days) is available as a paid add-on and requires procurement sign-off. Export costs depend on retained retention class (hot/warm/cold) — I'll have Neha attach the current rate card.

Please see the attached sample and playbook. If you want, we can schedule a 30-min run-through with your audit team next week to walk through the approval flow and validate the CSV schema.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Security & Compliance Liaison
Redwood Inference

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 11:21:00 -04:00
Subject: Internal: confirm export footprint + ticket tagging

Sofia / Neha — quick internal note before we reply with pricing:

- Confirm sample fields match our current export generator (I recall we added kv_cache_hit in June). If schema changed, include schema_version header.
- Ensure every ad-hoc export gets a metadata file: {ticket_id, approver, export_window, retention_class, export_sha256}. We should not send raw response payloads without explicit scope.
- For timebound access, the approver must be a security desk member and the approval token should be traceable in our audit system (JIRA SUP-987 tag).

Neha — please attach rate card and expected lead times for cold exports; flag any blackout windows for cross-region data egress.

Marissa
Director, Security Evidence

---

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Terry Alfaro <terry.alfaro@finbank.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Jul 2027 10:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: tenant log slices and short-lived access request

Hi Terry — attaching the rate card and a brief export SLT summary per your questions. Quick bullets below that mirror the attachments: 

- Sample export enclosed (redwood-audit-log-sample-202706.zip) — includes CSV + JSON schema + README. Schema_version: 2027-06-15-v2.
- Ephemeral access: supported. We issue one-time tokens tied to SUP tickets; audit metadata included in export manifest.
- Standard lead time for >180d exports: 10 business days; expedited: 2 business days (fee applies). No current cross-region blackout windows; we will notify if scheduled maintenance conflicts with requested windows.
- Costs: cold-export base fee USD 1,200 + per-GB retrieval. Expedited retrieval add-on: USD 2,500 flat.

Next steps: let me know which of these you want to validate first (sample schema walkthrough or process demo). I can set up a 30-min session and include an ops engineer to demo a live scoped export to a test S3 location.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Support Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood-audit-log-sample-202706.zip (CSV + schema README), timebound-access-playbook-v1.2.pdf (flow diagram + sample approval token).
